kept.excerpt: A total of three commodity vessels crossed the strait on Tuesday, down from four the previous day, Kpler data showed. There were no visible very large crude carrier (VLCC) or liquefied natural gas (LNG) tankers passing through the strait on Tuesday.
kept.relevance: Provides traffic observations for July 21 immediately before the experiment cutoff, although Kpler commodity-vessel counts are not the same measure as IMF PortWatch's all-covered-ship transit calls.

kept.excerpt: Maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has sharply declined in the past week (July 13-19) due to escalating security tensions, erasing previous gains from the US-Iran Memorandum of Understanding period. The US-backed southern Omani transit corridor is still in use with at least two tankers tracked using it during the week, but a high volume of dark transits makes it difficult to ascertain the route used in most cases.
kept.relevance: Establishes the recent direction of traffic and highlights visibility limitations that complicate comparisons between commercial tracking estimates and PortWatch's reported series.

kept.excerpt: Across 17–19 July, 13 crossings used the Iranian Unilateral Scheme, 14 were Route Undetermined, 2 used Omani Territorial Waters Passage and 1 used the Hormuz TSS.
kept.relevance: Provides a recent three-day breakdown of observed crossings and shows how little traffic was using the conventional traffic separation scheme.

kept.excerpt: These attacks further intensify the fear, uncertainty and psychological strain already being endured by the nearly 6,000 seafarers who remain stranded on board vessels unable to depart the Persian Gulf safely.
kept.relevance: Supplies official evidence that safety constraints and stranded vessels remained material obstacles to normal shipping before the cutoff.

kept.excerpt: Before U.S. and Israeli military operations began against Iran on February 28, 2026, the average number of ships from various countries transiting through the Strait of Hormuz (the Strait) was about 130 each day. As of April 7, 2026, only a handful of ships have risked the transit each day since the start of the operations for fear of attack by Iranian forces, which are reportedly negotiating with and permitting selected ships to pass through the Strait.
kept.publisher: Congressional Research Service, archived by EveryCRSReport
kept.relevance: Provides a dated historical baseline and an earlier disruption comparison, while its broad ship counts should not be treated as directly interchangeable with PortWatch's covered vessel categories.

kept.excerpt: PortWatch is an online platform designed to monitor and simulate disruptions to maritime trade due to climate extremes and other shocks. PortWatch uses satellite-based vessel data and big data analytics to help policymakers, analysts, and public stakeholders assess impacts of disruptions to maritime trade and simulate indirect spillover effects across the maritime network and global supply chains.
kept.relevance: Documents the official resolution provider's satellite-based measurement approach and supports distinguishing its reported indicator from other sources' physical-transit estimates.

search_notes: Frozen cutoff: 2026-07-22, inclusive. Included six distinct dated sources; excluded prediction-market pages, undated live dashboards, later publications, and retrospective data revisions. Publication dates and excerpts were checked against source text exposed in web_search results. Direct web_fetch failed because the environment had multiple fetch providers without an explicit selection; the requested agent-reach web read fallback returned RATE_LIMITED, so full-page retrieval could not be completed. No contemporaneous archived IMF PortWatch data vintage available by July 22 was verified; consequently this pack does not assert a PortWatch seven-day moving average as of the cutoff. Commercial tracker counts differ in vessel coverage, route attribution, and treatment of dark transits and must not be substituted directly for the resolution series. No post-cutoff developments or July 31 outcome are included.
